pricing.rule: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A pending/async ack or an unverifiable charged call (delivered:false, refundable:false) bills price_usd × 1.15 with no per-call fee; refunded calls, in-batch duplicates and failed runs bill $0. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

I’m just gonna rip thesis from mcg signal bc it explains borro better than I could but this is a genny infra spot

Borro is stock lending infrastructure on Robinhood Chain, where people lend out stock tokens or borrow USDG against them. Market makers and AI agents borrow those tokens to short them and pay the lender a fee while the short stays open. The team reports about $45,000 in TVL after about two weeks, and Raeto, an AI inference app on Robinhood Chain, made Borro its default deposit hub. 100% of platform fees go to buying and burning BORRO. Deposits stay capped until an audit, which creator fees are being saved to pay for.

comment.comment: $BORRO is a Robinhood Chain-based token enabling lending, borrowing, and shorting of stock tokens while earning rent on lent assets. Its micro-cap ($9.2K) and volatile price action (180% spikes) have drawn degenerate traders and meme coin communities, fueled by low liquidity ($4K) and high volatility. The token’s rapid spread mirrors speculative meme coin dynamics, amplified by crypto Twitter snipers tracking its charts and top holder clustering (22% supply concentrated). Its appeal lies in Robinhood’s retail-friendly branding and leveraged trading narratives, attracting high-risk gamblers. Community-shared charts and real-time metrics drive FOMO, though its sustainability hinges on broader adoption beyond pump cycles.
